subject: Provisional version lock & rollback-trigger approval for PayFlux canary
body:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Morris <elena@payflux.com>
Date: 2028-09-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: Provisional version lock & rollback-trigger approval for PayFlux canary

Team —

We're scheduled to run the PayFlux canary next Tue (2028-09-17). PayFlux has tight SLA clauses in the contract (99.95% uptime / 95th pct latency targets). Legal asked us to document a formal mitigation for potential regressions during the canary: specifically, a provisional version lock (pin) and an automatic rollback trigger that will be allowed as an exception to normal release policy for this deal (PF-4921).

Request: please confirm (by EOD Mon) whether we can approve the following operational guardrails for this canary:

- Provisional version lock (pin): if enabled, block new model variant promotion for the PayFlux traffic route for up to 72 hours post-rollout unless explicitly unpinned by Platform Ops.
- Auto-rollback trigger: on breach of any of the configured gating metrics (listed below), automatically swap traffic back to the last-stable variant and pin for 24 hours.
- Gating metrics: 5 min sustained error rate > 0.5%, 95th percentile latency spike > 250ms above baseline for > 10 minutes, or token-cost per request > 2x baseline for 15 minutes.
- Observability: require trace-id propagation and immediate PagerDuty alert to SRE, plus a strike recorded in the rollback matrix (attached).

Attachments: payflux_prod_metrics.csv (baseline) and provisional_rollback_matrix.xlsx (decision matrix & playbook).

Why this is needed: PayFlux has business-critical latency constraints on their checkout flow. The canary is low-volume (1% traffic) but the SLA carveout in the contract requires explicit mitigation to avoid escalation to customer ops or credits. Approving the provisional lock + auto-rollback is the cleanest way to offer an SLA-level assurance without manual gating every minute.

Please reply with any objections or changes. If SRE (Kimberly) approves, Laura can sign the operational exemption. Aditya — flag for sales that this is an approved exception we can show PayFlux if they ask.

Thanks,
Sean
--
Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Reliability (Sales Engineering Lead)
Redwood Inference

---

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Morris <elena@payflux.com>
Date: 2028-09-10T12:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Provisional version lock & rollback-trigger approval for PayFlux canary

Thanks Sean —

I think the proposal is reasonable as an SLA mitigation, but I have a couple of asks before I sign off:

1) Can we tighten the auto-rollback window to make sure we don't oscillate on transient noise? Suggest: require two consecutive 5-min windows breaching the threshold (i.e., 10 continuous minutes) before triggering.
2) Add a manual override path for the customer-facing on-call (so if PayFlux is observing false positives we can coordinate).
3) Confirm that pin/unpin actions are auditable (who clicked what and when) and retained for 12 months for contract/audit purposes.

If Kimberly confirms the telemetry gating and Aditya confirms Sales is comfortable with the wording we'll approve.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Operations
Redwood Inference

---

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Elena Morris <elena@payflux.com>
Date: 2028-09-11T08:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Provisional version lock & rollback-trigger approval for PayFlux canary

Confirming SRE input. TL;DR: we can support the provisional version lock + auto-rollback with the following operational controls in place:

- Debounce: auto-rollback will require two consecutive 5-minute windows (10 minutes total) of breach to avoid flapping.
- Safe-fallback variant: rollback will target the last-stable variant (immutable tag) and will reduce traffic to 0% for the canary cohort for 2 minutes while health checks revalidate, then return to 0% steady state.
- Customer-visible behavior: the swap is transparent — requests already routed will finish on the variant they started on; new requests will be routed to the stable variant. No payload rewrites.
- Audit & retention: pin/unpin and rollback actions will be logged in the Console audit trail (user, timestamp, reason) and exported to the contract audit bucket (retained 13 months).
- Kill switch: manual 'kill' (complete suspend) is available if the auto-rollback isn't sufficient; only Platform Ops and Laura's org can execute.

I attached a provisional rollback matrix (provisional_rollback_matrix.xlsx) with exact thresholds and escalation steps. We should also add a short runbook link to the console deploy page. If Sales wants an explicit customer-facing confirmation, Aditya should coordinate with Elena to publish a brief note that explains what 'auto-rollback' means operationally.

Kimberly Park
Senior SRE
Redwood Inference

---

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Morris <elena@payflux.com>, ops@payflux.com
Date: 2028-09-12T11:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Provisional version lock & rollback-trigger approval for PayFlux canary

Thanks all — good alignment. Summary / action items we agreed: 

- Auto-rollback debounce: require 2x 5-min windows (10 continuous minutes) before triggering.
- Rollback target: last-stable immutable variant; traffic to canary set to 0% after swap; 2-minute quick health validation.
- Pin durations: provisional pin for 72h on promotion; post-rollback pin for 24h pending root-cause.
- Audit & retention: logs retained 13 months; Console will record user & timestamp.
- Manual overrides: kill switch available to Platform Ops + Laura's org; customer override path for PayFlux on-call coordinated by Aditya.

Aditya — please confirm with PayFlux that this behavior meets their expectation and whether they want us to include a short customer-facing summary. If no objections from PayFlux, Laura will sign the operational exemption doc and we'll publish the change to the deploy console for PF-4921.

Elena — tagging you to confirm if those thresholds and the transparent rollback semantics match PayFlux needs.

I'll update the canary plan doc and push the rollout with these defaults unless I hear objections by EOD Mon (2028-09-18).

Sean
--
Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Reliability (Sales Engineering Lead)
Redwood Inference

[Attachments referenced: payflux_prod_metrics.csv (baseline metrics snapshot), provisional_rollback_matrix.xlsx (decision matrix & runbook)]
